top_choice_rationale: P001 honours the Kane-Mele prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators together with Molenkamp's HgTe realization. The result is conceptually new relative to the 2016 prize, has been reproduced over about two decades, and is the only shortlisted candidate where a theory-plus-experiment three-name split follows the logic of the discovery. The citation must stay limited to the two-dimensional state so that it does not imply credit for the omitted Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan contributions. P002 (optical lattice clocks, Katori and Ye) is mature and cleanly attributed, but it overlaps the metrology prizes of 2005 and 2012 and its priority claims cannot be fully checked. It is a sound second choice, and an award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Professional proximity to the superconducting-circuit community (Chalmers colleagues of the 2025 laureates, WACQT) bears on B010, which is not in the slate; no specific connection to the credited names in P001 or P002 is apparent from profile.
